checklist: cert/version.mjs: az version is exactly azure-cli <homescoop.upstream>, azure-cli-core and azure-cli-telemetry at the versions of their .dist-info, no extensions, and nothing on stderr; az --version names Python (wasi) 3.15 and the config directory; a first az group list --debug takes upstream's packaged command index (commandIndex.latest.json) and loads only azure.cli.command_modules.resource, with no SyntaxWarning

cert/login.mjs: against a stand-in for Entra ID and ARM behind the kernel's proxy (TLS with the kernel CA): plain az login (can-launch-browser-wasi.patch) and az login --use-device-code print Entra ID's 'open https://login.microsoft.com/device and enter the code' message, never localhost; az asks for the device code with its own client id and the management scope, polls the token endpoint with the device code, lists tenants and subscriptions with the token; az account show, az group list (Bearer token on the ARM call) and az account get-access-token from the cached login; msal_token_cache.json is plain JSON, mode 0600, with the refresh token; az logout empties az account list

cert/sp.mjs: az login --service-principal with a client secret (the client_credentials grant) and with a federated token (client_assertion), az group list with that token, az account get-access-token; service_principal_entries.json mode 0600; a wrong secret is Entra ID's AADSTS7000215 without a traceback; certificate login, az keyvault list and az webapp list exit 1 with one ERROR line naming pyOpenSSL, cryptography and PyNaCl and no traceback (the launcher's NativeFinder)

cert/storage.mjs (storage-encryption-without-cryptography.patch): az storage account list (ARM), and az storage blob list, upload and download with an account key against a stand-in for certacct.blob.core.windows.net, every request signed SharedKey; the patched blob and queue _encryption modules raise ModuleNotFoundError for cryptography when client-side encryption is used

cert/config.mjs: az config get shows core.collect_telemetry=no, core.survey_message=no, extension.use_dynamic_install=no, core.first_run=yes and core.encrypt_token_cache=false from the launcher's environment; bare az shows the welcome without the telemetry notice; no telemetry or az_survey.json files, also in a terminal; az ssh vm (an extension's command) is not found, with no request; az config set survey_message, use_dynamic_install and encrypt_token_cache: the first two win (az_survey.json appears in a terminal), encrypt_token_cache stays false; a caller's environment wins too

cert/launcher.mjs: a shadowing yaml (imported at startup by a .pth) and a fake cryptography in wasix-python's site-packages: a plain python3 gets them, az doesn't (az group list -o yaml works, az keyvault list names the missing cryptography); AZURE_CLI_SITEPACKAGES=1 puts site-packages back after az's own; TLS through the proxy works with CURL_CA_BUNDLE unset (REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE from SSL_CERT_FILE); a caller's REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE wins; the launcher under another name exits 1

cert/extension.mjs: az extension add --source of a pure-Python extension wheel made in the kernel installs it with wasix-python's pip into ~/.azure/cliextensions; its command runs, az version lists it, az extension remove takes it out

cert/notices.mjs (homescoop#2112): THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md has a '## <distribution> <version> (<SPDX>)' section with License: and the license text (the notices harness's checkNotices with the built-in phrase; for ANTLR, whose text reads 'Neither name of', that sentence) for each distribution whose wheel ships no license file: antlr4-python3-runtime and isodate (BSD-3-Clause), asn1crypto, wcwidth and the 17 older azure-* packages (MIT), as licenses.map gives them (read by the spec itself, not meta.json notices: nothing here is linked into a wasm)

test/files.test.mjs (host, the test job): wheels.lock is for the recipe release and the recipe's requirements sha256, and lib/azure-cli has exactly its distributions at its versions; the ten excluded packages and pycparser are absent; no __pycache__, .pyc, native code, .exe, links or <dist>.data; the packaged command and help index for the release; both patches applied; bin/az is src/launcher.py, 0755, the only command; LICENSE is azure-cli's; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md lists every distribution and every license file it names exists

by hand, not in CI (the cert kernel has no network, CI has no Azure credentials): on slicc-kernel 1.189.2's Node entry with wasm-tls-engine and nodeTransport(), against the real Entra ID: az login --use-device-code and plain az login print a real code for https://login.microsoft.com/device; az --version reached azcliprod.blob.core.windows.net ('Your CLI is up-to-date.'); a service principal login reached the tenant's token endpoint (AADSTS700026 for a made-up app id). The human sign-in with the code was not done

patches.can-launch-browser-wasi.patch: azure-cli-core's can_launch_browser() checks for a browser on WASI as on Linux, so plain az login falls back to the device code flow; without it az says a browser was opened and waits for a localhost redirect (login.mjs times out, NEGATIVE.md)
azure-storage-blob, -queue and -common import cryptography in a try, so the SDKs load without it; without it every az storage command, az storage account list included, fails with TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable (storage.mjs, NEGATIVE.md)
